$comment: Generated by gh-settings 0.2.0. Do not edit by hand; run `gh settings schema`.

is_alphanumeric.description:
Whether the reference is alphanumeric rather than purely numeric.

Defaults to `true`, matching GitHub. Set to `false` for systems whose
identifiers are always numbers.

key_prefix.description:
The prefix that triggers the link, for example `OPS-`.

This is the autolink's identity: changing it creates a new autolink rather
than modifying the existing one.

url_template.description:
Target URL, containing the `<num>` placeholder.

For example `https://jira.company.com/browse/<num>`.

oneOf.description: GitHub builds the site from a branch, with its own Jekyll pipeline.
The site is published by an Actions workflow.

BypassActor.description:
Who may bypass a ruleset.

Declared by slug rather than id: numeric ids are neither stable across
organisations nor meaningful to a human reading the file, which would make an
exported configuration unusable anywhere but its origin. Resolution happens in
[`Resource::prepare`](crate::resources::Resource::prepare).

actor_id.description:
Raw actor identifier.

An escape hatch for actor kinds this build does not model by name, such as
repository roles, whose identifiers vary between organisations and so
cannot be safely mapped from a name.

actor_type.description: Raw actor type, used together with `actor_id`.

app.description: Bypass through a GitHub App, by slug.

team.description: Bypass through an organisation team, by slug.

BypassMode.description: When a bypass actor may bypass the ruleset.

Conditions.description: Which refs a ruleset applies to.

anyOf.description: Only branches with protection rules or a matching ruleset.
Explicit branch and tag name patterns.

branches.description: Branch name patterns, for example `main` or `release/*`.

DeploymentBranchPolicy.description: Which refs may deploy to an environment.

Enforcement.description: How strictly a ruleset is applied.

oneOf.description: Evaluated and reported, but not enforced. Requires GitHub Enterprise.

deployment_branch_policy.description:
Which refs may deploy to this environment.

Three states, and the difference between the last two matters: omitting
the field leaves the policy alone, whereas an explicit `null` sets it to
*any branch*, which is GitHub's own default and a real setting.

```yaml
deployment_branch_policy: protected      # protected branches only
deployment_branch_policy:                # explicit patterns
  branches: [main, "release/*"]
  tags: ["v*"]
deployment_branch_policy: null           # any branch
```

name.description:
The environment name, for example `production`.

GitHub matches names case-insensitively, so `Production` and
`production` are the same environment. Names may contain spaces and
slashes.

prevent_self_review.description:
Whether the user who triggered a deployment may approve it themselves.

Only meaningful alongside `reviewers`: with nobody to review, there is
no approval to prevent.

reviewers.description:
Who must approve a deployment to this environment.

Omitted leaves reviewers unmanaged; an empty list removes them all.

variables.description:
Actions variables scoped to this environment.

Omitting the key leaves the environment's variables unmanaged; an empty
list declares that it should have none. Whether unmanaged variables are
deleted is governed by the `environments` section's `prune` flag, since
a variable cannot be pruned independently of the environment holding it.

wait_timer.description:
Minutes to wait before a deployment to this environment may proceed.

Between 0 and 43200 (30 days). Zero and an omitted timer are the same
state to GitHub, so setting it back to zero removes the rule.

color.description:
Six hexadecimal digits, with or without a leading `#`.

Normalised to lowercase without the `#`, which is how GitHub stores it.

description.description: Optional short description, at most 100 characters.

name.description:
Label name.

When `new_name` is set, this is the name the label currently has.

new_name.description:
Rename this label to the given name.

Renaming preserves the label's assignments, which deleting and recreating
would not.

PagesSettings.description:
The `pages` configuration section.

Declaring the section enables GitHub Pages if it is off. It never turns Pages
back off: an omitted section means *unmanaged*, so there is no way to express
"disabled", and destroying a published site is not something a missing key
should do (ADR-005).

```yaml
pages:
  build_type: workflow
  cname: docs.example.com
  https_enforced: true
```

build_type.description: How the site is built: from a branch (`legacy`) or by a workflow.

cname.description:
Custom domain for the site.

Set to `null` to remove it and fall back to the `github.io` address.

https_enforced.description:
Whether HTTP requests are redirected to HTTPS.

GitHub refuses to enable this until it has provisioned a certificate for
the custom domain, which can take a while after `cname` is first set. A
`sync` that sets both at once may need running twice.

source.description:
Branch and directory to publish from.

Only meaningful with `build_type: legacy`; GitHub rejects a source sent
for a workflow-built site.

```yaml
source:
  branch: gh-pages
  path: /docs
```

ProtectedKeyword.description: The only word accepted where a policy keyword is expected.

anyOf.description: Bare list form. Additive: unmanaged items are left alone.
Object form, able to enable pruning.

items.description:
The declared items.

Modelled as an `Option` rather than a defaulted `Vec` so the section
does not require its item type to implement `Default`.

prune.description:
Delete items that exist on GitHub but are absent here.

Defaults to `false`. Overridden by `--prune` / `--no-prune`.

Prunable.description: A collection section that can opt into pruning.

include.description:
Patterns to include.

Supports the special values `~DEFAULT_BRANCH` and `~ALL`.

allow_auto_merge.description: Whether auto-merge is available on pull requests.

allow_update_branch.description: Whether updating a pull request branch is allowed.

anonymous_access_enabled.description: Whether anonymous Git read access is enabled (GitHub Enterprise only).

archived.description:
Whether the repository is archived.

Archiving is effectively one-way through the API: GitHub allows setting
this to `true`, but unarchiving must be done in the web UI.

default_branch.description:
The default branch.

Renames the branch; it must already exist.

delete_branch_on_merge.description: Whether head branches are deleted automatically after merge.

description.description:
Short description shown under the repository name.

Set to `null` to clear it.

has_discussions.description: Whether the discussions tab is enabled.

has_issues.description: Whether the issue tracker is enabled.

homepage.description:
Project website shown next to the description.

Set to `null` to clear it.

is_template.description: Whether the repository is a template.

merge_commit_message.description: Default commit message for merge commits.

merge_commit_title.description: Default commit title for merge commits.

private.description:
Whether the repository is private.

Changing this is possible but consequential — it can delete forks and
break published links — so `plan` always flags it.

squash_merge_commit_message.description: Default commit message for squash merges.

squash_merge_commit_title.description: Default commit title for squash merges.

topics.description:
Topics.

Accepted here only for `safe-settings` compatibility; prefer the
top-level `topics` section.

Reviewer.description:
Who must approve a deployment.

Declared by login or slug rather than by numeric identifier: identifiers are
neither stable across organisations nor meaningful to a human, which would
make an exported configuration useless anywhere but its origin. Resolution
to identifiers happens in `prepare`, before anything is written.

Rule.description:
A single rule within a ruleset.

Modelled as `{ type, parameters }` rather than a closed enum of every known
rule so that a rule type this build predates round-trips untouched instead of
being silently dropped.

type.description: The rule type, for example `pull_request` or `required_status_checks`.

name.description:
Ruleset name.

This is the identity used for matching. Server ids never appear in the
configuration because they are not portable between repositories.

SecuritySettings.description:
Security and analysis features.

The API models these as `{ status: "enabled" | "disabled" }` objects rather
than booleans; the configuration exposes plain booleans and the resource
translates.

Source.description: The branch and directory a `legacy` build publishes from.

branch.description: Branch the site is published from, for example `gh-pages`.

path.description:
Directory within the branch, either `/` or `/docs`.

GitHub supports no other value. Written without the leading slash it is
added for you, so `docs` and `/docs` mean the same thing.

oneOf.description: The commit messages of the branch.
The commit title, when the pull request has a single commit.
Pushes, including to repositories without branches yet.

name.description:
The variable name, for example `DEPLOY_URL`.

GitHub uppercases names and matches them case-insensitively, so `api_url`
and `API_URL` are the same variable. Names may contain only letters,
digits and underscores, may not start with a digit, and may not start
with `GITHUB_`.

value.description:
The value.

Stored and compared verbatim: leading and trailing whitespace is
significant, because a workflow will see exactly what is written here.

description: Declarative GitHub repository settings, managed by the `gh settings` CLI extension.

environments.description:
Deployment environments and their protection rules.

Environment-scoped Actions variables are declared inside each
environment, under `variables`.

Note that inheritance replaces an environment whole: a file that extends
another and redeclares `production` merely to change its `wait_timer`
also replaces the inherited `variables` and `reviewers` lists.

extends.description:
Inherit this configuration from another repository.

Written as `owner/repo[/path/to/file]@ref`. The path is optional and
defaults to `.github/settings.yml`, so:

- `acme/.github@v1` reads `.github/settings.yml` from `acme/.github`
- `acme/.github/config/base.yml@v1` reads that file instead

The ref is required, so a shared base cannot move underneath a plan that
was reviewed against it.

Anything the local file declares wins. Collections are merged by item
identity — a label of the same name replaces the inherited one outright —
and `prune` is never inherited, so editing a shared file cannot start
deleting things in the repositories that extend it.

A base configuration may not itself use `extends`.

pages.description:
GitHub Pages.

Declaring this section enables Pages if it is off. It never turns Pages
off again: an omitted section means unmanaged, so there is nothing to
express "disabled" with.

repository.description:
Repository metadata: description, homepage, features, merge and security
settings.

topics.description:
Repository topics.

Also accepted under `repository.topics` for `safe-settings`
compatibility; declaring both is an error.

variables.description:
Repository-scoped Actions variables.

Environment-scoped variables live under `environments[].variables`
instead.

version.description: Schema major version this file targets.
